subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A motor unit is best defined as:
options: A single muscle fibre and its mitochondria
A group of muscles working as antagonists
A motor neurone and all the muscle fibres it stimulates
questions.explain: A motor unit comprises a single motor neurone and all the muscle fibres it innervates.

questions.q: On a force-time graph for a foot strike in running, a net positive impulse indicates the runner is:
questions.explain: A net positive impulse means a net forward force over time, increasing momentum and accelerating the runner.

questions.q: Erythropoietin (EPO) is a banned ergogenic aid because it:
options: Stimulates red blood cell production, increasing oxygen-carrying capacity
questions.explain: EPO increases erythrocyte production, raising oxygen transport, but also dangerously increases blood viscosity.

questions.q: Performing prolonged exercise in hot conditions primarily challenges the body by:
options: Causing dehydration and competing demands for blood flow between muscles and skin
questions.explain: In the heat, blood is diverted to the skin for cooling while muscles also demand it, and sweating risks dehydration.

questions.q: For a power athlete loading before competition, the most appropriate dietary manipulation is:
options: Carbohydrate loading over three days with depletion
Creatine supplementation to boost PC stores
questions.explain: Creatine supplementation increases phosphocreatine stores, benefiting short, high-intensity power efforts.

questions.q: A first-class lever in the body has the:
options: Fulcrum between the effort and the load
questions.explain: A first-class lever has the fulcrum between the effort and the load, as at the elbow during extension or the neck.

questions.q: Which ion is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum to trigger muscle contraction?
questions.explain: Calcium ions bind to troponin, moving tropomyosin and exposing actin binding sites for cross-bridge formation.

questions.q: Which muscle-fibre type is best suited to a marathon runner?
questions.explain: Type I slow oxidative fibres are highly fatigue-resistant and aerobic, ideal for endurance events.

questions.q: Three factors that determine the horizontal distance of a projectile are speed of release, angle of release and:
questions.explain: Speed of release, angle of release and height of release together determine the horizontal distance travelled.

questions.q: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of:
questions.explain: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time (change in velocity ÷ time taken).

questions.q: A sprinter pushing back and down on the blocks, and being driven forwards and up, best illustrates Newton's:
questions.explain: Newton's third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, generating the ground reaction force.

questions.q: Which respiratory adaptation results from long-term aerobic training?
options: Increased strength of respiratory muscles and greater gas exchange efficiency
questions.explain: Training strengthens respiratory muscles and improves the efficiency of pulmonary gas exchange.

questions.q: Moment of inertia depends on a body's mass and:
options: The distribution of mass relative to the axis of rotation
questions.explain: Moment of inertia is determined by mass and how that mass is distributed about the axis of rotation.

questions.q: Myoglobin's main role in muscle is to:
options: Store and transport oxygen within the muscle fibre
questions.explain: Myoglobin stores oxygen in muscle and releases it to the mitochondria for aerobic respiration.

questions.q: Weight as a force acts:
options: Vertically downwards through the centre of mass
Horizontally in the direction of motion
Perpendicular to the reaction force only
questions.explain: Weight is the gravitational force acting vertically downwards through a body's centre of mass.

questions.q: Cardiac output is correctly calculated as:
questions.explain: Cardiac output (Q) equals stroke volume multiplied by heart rate.

questions.q: The 'all-or-none' law of muscle contraction means that:
options: If a motor unit fires, all its fibres contract maximally
All muscle fibres in the body contract together
Force is graded within a single fibre
questions.explain: When a motor unit is stimulated above threshold, all of its fibres contract maximally, or none do.

questions.q: Torque (the moment of a force) is calculated as:
options: Force × perpendicular distance from the axis
questions.explain: Torque, or moment, equals the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.

questions.q: The oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve has an S (sigmoid) shape. A shift to the RIGHT means haemoglobin:
options: Has a greater affinity for oxygen
Releases oxygen more readily to tissues
Binds more oxygen at the lungs
questions.explain: A right shift lowers haemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, so oxygen is unloaded more readily at the tissues.

questions.q: According to the Bernoulli principle, where air flows faster over a surface:
questions.explain: Bernoulli's principle states that faster-moving air exerts lower pressure, creating lift or directional forces.

questions.q: The Magnus effect explains how a spinning ball:
options: Swerves or dips because of a pressure difference created by the spin
questions.explain: Spin creates differing air velocities and pressures on each side of the ball (Magnus effect), producing a swerve or dip.

questions.q: According to the sliding-filament theory, muscle shortening occurs when:
options: Actin filaments slide over myosin, pulled by cross-bridges
questions.explain: Myosin cross-bridges attach to actin and pull the actin filaments inwards, shortening the sarcomere.

questions.q: A long jumper increasing the time over which the take-off force is applied will, for a given force:
options: Increase the change in momentum and so the velocity at take-off
questions.explain: By the impulse-momentum relationship, a larger impulse (force × time) produces a greater change in momentum and velocity.

questions.q: Starling's law of the heart states that stroke volume increases when there is greater:
options: Sympathetic stimulation of the SA node
questions.explain: Greater venous return stretches the ventricle walls, increasing the force of contraction and stroke volume.

questions.q: During the cardiac conduction sequence, after the AV node the impulse passes to the:
questions.explain: The impulse passes from the AV node down the bundle of His before reaching the Purkinje fibres.

questions.q: A chronic cardiovascular adaptation to endurance training is:
options: Cardiac hypertrophy and increased resting stroke volume
questions.explain: Endurance training enlarges the heart (hypertrophy), raising stroke volume and lowering resting heart rate (bradycardia).

questions.q: During a 100 m sprint lasting around 10 seconds, the predominant energy system is the:
questions.explain: Maximal efforts up to about 10 seconds are fuelled predominantly by the ATP-PC system.

questions.q: The vertical velocity component of a projectile at the highest point of its flight is:
questions.explain: At the peak of flight the vertical velocity is momentarily zero before gravity accelerates the object downwards.

questions.q: Angular velocity is the rate of change of:
questions.explain: Angular velocity is angular displacement divided by the time taken, measured in radians per second.

questions.q: The net force acting on a body is:
options: The resultant of all forces acting on the body
The force of air resistance alone
questions.explain: Net (resultant) force is the overall vector sum of all forces acting on a body, determining its acceleration.
